steps.title: Opposition Testing
steps.markdown:
This tutorial will guide you through activating one leg of the OwnTech TWIST board and setting a fixed duty cycle.

To begin, open the **Courseware** menu in the top menu bar, then go to **Hackathons → Opposition Testing**.

> **Tip:** Maximize the application window so all panels are fully visible.

steps.title: Upload the firmware
steps.markdown:
In the Opposition Testing panel:

1. Select your board's port from the **Target port** dropdown (click **Refresh** if the list is empty).
2. Click **Upload document to target** to flash the opposition-testing firmware.

Wait for the upload to finish before continuing.

steps.title: Load the dashboard
steps.markdown: Click **Load document dashboard** to load the pre-built Opposition Testing layout into the workspace.

steps.title: Power on
steps.markdown: In the **Action Buttons** pane, click **POWER ON** to enable the power stage.

steps.title: Enable LEG1
steps.markdown:
In the **Action Buttons** pane, find the **Leg toggles** section.

Under the **LEG1** row, enable the **LEG** switch.

> **Tip:** If you cannot see the LEG1 row, maximize the window — the Action Buttons pane may be scrolled out of view.

steps.title: Enable DRIVER1
steps.markdown: Still under the **LEG1** row in the Leg toggles section, enable the **DRIVER** switch to start the gate driver for leg 1.

steps.title: Set duty cycle to 0.5
steps.markdown:
In the **Setpoint Buttons** pane under **LEG1**, find the **Duty** row:

1. Type **0.5** in the duty input field.
2. Click **Send**.

The converter will run at 50% duty cycle.

steps.title: Tutorial complete
steps.markdown:
You have successfully activated one leg of the TWIST board!

- LEG1 is enabled with its gate driver running.
- The duty cycle is set to 0.5 (50%).

You can now adjust setpoints or enable the second leg in the same way. Close this tutorial when you are done.
